body.statement:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), \(n=|V|\), \(M=|\Omega|\), and
\[
 b_{\tau}=8(n+1)^2\left\lceil\log_2(n+L+M+2)\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 B_{\mathrm{sw}}=M\bigl(m+L+M+n(1+L)+b_{\tau}\bigr).
\]
If the oracle-instance is feasible, it has a lexicographically canonical accepting switching certificate with at most \(M\) nonempty singleton-ownership records, no empty-ownership record, at most \(M\) distinct protocols, and cost no larger than that of any accepting acquired collection.  Every transcript has at most \(n\) strict restrictions and at most \(b_{\tau}\) bits, so its exact length satisfies \(N_{\mathrm{sw}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  Consequently the lexicographically first minimum-cost switching certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\) exists and satisfies \(N_{E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  The branch count \(M\), and hence \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\), may be exponential in the structural input; no \(k\)-record or polynomial certificate bound is claimed.  Oracle replies remain separately charged by \(N_{\mathcal O}\).
body.proof_tex:
Let \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) be any accepted switching certificate.  First discard every empty-ownership record.  Such a record supplies no branch witness, so acceptance is unchanged; deleting its protocol can only decrease cost because every \(c(a)\) is nonnegative.  Next split a record owning a set \(K\subseteq\Omega\) into \(|K|\) records with the same protocol--slice--source triple, one for each \(\alpha\in K\).  Distinct-protocol charging implies that this operation leaves cost unchanged.  Since the ownership sets partition \(\Omega\), retain the resulting exactly \(M\) singleton-ownership records; no coalescing is needed or valid because their ownership masks differ.

For each successful owned branch, Proposition \(\mathrm{Fixed\ factor\ obstruction}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) give a canonical transcript with at most \(|T|\leq n\) strict restrictions.  Encode every vertex set by its \(n\)-bit incidence mask.  At each restriction there are at most three such masks and a constant number of delimiters and identifiers; every identifier is drawn from a set of size at most \(n+L+M+2\).  Across at most \(n\) restrictions, padding to \(8(n+1)^2\) identifier-sized fields therefore gives the valid upper bound
\[
 |\operatorname{enc}(\tau_{\alpha})|
 \leq 8(n+1)^2\left\lceil\log_2(n+L+M+2)\right\rceil=b_{\tau}.                 \tag{4}
\]
Graph reachability, bidirected connectivity, and literal equality are recomputed from the structural input, so no unlisted path or law value is hidden in (4).

A singleton-ownership switching record contains an \(m\)-bit protocol mask, an \(L\)-bit slice mask, an \(M\)-bit branch mask, an \(n(1+L)\)-bit labelled-source mask, and one transcript.  Hence
\[
 N_{\mathrm{sw}}
 \leq M\bigl(m+L+M+n(1+L)+b_{\tau}\bigr)=B_{\mathrm{sw}}.                    \tag{5}
\]
Sorting records and choosing the lexicographically first canonical transcript make the encoding canonical.

Now suppose a generic acquired collection \(E_0\) is accepted.  The switching normal-form theorem produces an accepted switching certificate of cost at most \(\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)\), and the preceding canonicalization preserves acceptance, satisfies (5), and does not increase cost.  Thus, for every accepting \(E_0\), at least one accepted binary string of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\) has no larger cost.

There are fewer than \(2^{B_{\mathrm{sw}}+1}\) binary strings of length at most \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  The accepted canonical subset is therefore finite.  If the instance is feasible it is nonempty, and exact binary-rational costs have a minimum on it; lexicographic order breaks ties.  Call the resulting certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\).  The domination just proved shows that its cost is no larger than that of any accepting generic acquisition, while (5) gives \(N_{E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}}\leq B_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  Finally, \(M\) is a Cartesian-product branch count, so it need not be polynomial in \(N_{\mathrm{in}}\); the proof yields no such bound.
body.justification: The bound exposes every branch-ownership bit and concrete transcript while keeping oracle support payload separate.
body.gap: No published fixed-source result bounds a priced physical switching certificate.
body.consumer: The exact search has a finite radius \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\), which may be exponential.
